A request that changes only some fields of an existing record on the server.

sections.name: File setup
sections.title: Imports for the packet page
sections.what: Brings in the tools, components, data types, and labels needed to load, edit, and show a review packet.
sections.why: Needed for loading the packet, handling the address, and showing the right language.

sections.name: PacketContent
sections.title: Loading, creating, and saving the packet
sections.what: Loads an existing packet or creates one from a verification result. It also saves the notes and request text, and can mark the packet ready for review. Messages report success or failure.
sections.why: Lets the user prepare the packet in steps, with saving at any point.
sections.watch_out: Saved text is what the user typed, not the translated text shown when the request has not been edited.

sections.name: ReviewPacketPage
sections.title: Packet page entry point
sections.what: Reads the packet or result id from the address and passes it to the content. The content is re-created when that id changes.
sections.why: Makes sure the page reloads the correct packet when the address changes.
sections.watch_out: If the address changes without a new id, the old packet may stay on screen.

summary: Lets the user open, edit, and save a review packet, which is a summary of the case prepared for a reviewer.
purpose: Helps the user write the notes and review request for a case and mark the packet ready for review.
why: Likely reason: a packet can be opened by its id, or created from a verification result, so the page handles both ways.
how: If the address includes a packet id, it loads that packet. If it includes a result id instead, it creates a new packet and then updates the address to show the packet id. The user can edit notes and request text, save them, or save and mark the packet ready for review.
inputs: The packet or result id from the address, the case id, the typed notes and request text, and the chosen language.
outputs: A loaded or newly created packet, saved edits, status messages, and an updated packet status.
risks: The request text shown may be a translated version when the user has not edited it. What gets saved is the typed text, so the saved text and the displayed text can differ. Loading errors show a message, but the packet is not shown.
debug: If the message says the packet failed, check the packet endpoints and their responses. If saved text looks different from what was shown, compare the typed text with the translated display. If the address does not update after creating a packet, check the replace step.
